unsupported_claims: Classical methods are limited by needing the whole graph up front (the paper emphasizes quadratic time complexity, not this requirement).

DeepWalk can build the Hierarchical Softmax tree without seeing the entire graph when vertex frequencies follow a power-law distribution (the paper's condition is that the cardinality of V is known or can be bounded).

The Huffman-coded tree is built from observed frequencies, enabling online operation (the paper builds the tree for a maximum vertex count and uses Huffman coding only if frequencies can be estimated a priori).
rationale: The answer gets the classical-method limitation only vaguely (costly and poorly scaling, but not the quadratic complexity) and adds an unsupported 'needs whole graph' claim. Its core claim about DeepWalk, a power-law frequency condition, contradicts the source, which requires that the cardinality of V be known or boundable.
